rv.q: Whiteside's deeply moving performance is so multi-layered and, frankly, courageous as to more than compensate.
In the last third of the play, mayhem breaks loose, and you will be stunned, shocked and glued to your seat by the culmination of this stunning drama.
This is a powerful drama that cuts deep; it’s easy to recommend and difficult to watch, but watch it, you must.
This production reminds you why Come Back, Little Sheba mattered in 1950—and why, in the right hands, it still matters now.
But seeing the ways in which Lola, in particular, is trapped and trying to make the best of things feels absolutely heartbreaking in Whiteside's perfectly understated but richly detailed performance.
It remains an honest and compelling examination of one of society's great ills.
This play is a reminder for many of us of what American life was like before microwave ovens, online classes and streaming on television.
ABT’s claustrophobically intense and uninterrupted production, while not perfect, delivers that message with force and feeling.
ABT's production, in their intimate Studio , smoothly directed by Elyse Dolan, is a powerful 90 minutes of theater.
Come Back, Little Sheba is a very moving play and will make you feel a lot of emotions as American Blues paints this picture of this time period in America for us.

cn.t: American Blues Theater's intimate revival of Inge's classic earns praise for exceptional performances, particularly Whiteside's, and immersive staging. Critics find the production tight and powerful, proving the 1950 drama still resonates.
